newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel says 1996 sales up but profits weaker.
newsitem.headline: Opel says 1996 sales up but profits weaker.

text.p: Adam Opel AG, the German unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, said on Thursday its 1996 sales rose 9.3 percent to 28.3 billion marks, the second highest level in company history.
But Opel said it expected the 1996 profit to be between 250 and 350 million marks, below the 1995 level of 363 million marks, and predicted tough industry conditions for 1997.
"We are satisfied with the results when viewed against the background of stiff competition and difficult conditions in 1996," Opel chief executive David Herman said in a statement.
But Herman warned of difficult industry conditions in 1997, saying Opel expected a lower rate of market growth and at the same time pressure on sales, profit and vehicle deliveries.
He said the carmaker would intensify its efforts on reducing costs to improve productivity but did not say whether the carmaker planned any job cuts.
Opel's workforce in 1996 was cut by 867 positions to 44,695 workers.

Opel said 1996 revenues were boosted by strong sales increases for its Vectra saloon as well as production of the Catera, a modified version of its Omega saloon, for export to the United States under the Cadillac brand.

Opel, which last month ended its bitter dispute with Volkswagen AG over allegations of industrial spying by its German rival, also said its results were helped by the weaker mark, making exports more favourable.
The carmaker said it produced 1.18 million units last year, up from 1.14 million in 1995. Production included about 876,000 vehicles and 306,000 parts.
At its modern production plant in Eisenach, Opel said vehicle production was slightly higher in 1996 at 162,000 vehicles compared with 160,000 in 1995.
Including the GM-owned Vauxhall brand sold in Britain, Opel said GM's European production reached a new record at 1.84 million units, a 2.5 percent increase over 1995.
For 1997, Herman said the carmaker would become the first European manufacturer to offer a three-cylinder engine, which will be first offered in the Corsa subcompact model.
